subject: tech
title: On, Off and Logging In
about: Turning a device on and off and logging in: the power button, starting up, holding the button to shut down, a quick press for sleep (dark screen, still on), waking it, the charging light, what logging in means, a grown-up's face or finger unlock, the lock screen, logging out so nobody else can use your account, a kid account versus a grown-up account, shut down versus sleep, and checking your work is saved before the lid closes. NC K2-IC-04 (responsible login and logoff procedures on all devices) and K2-CS-03 (operate software). Read it together and let him do the real log in and log out on his own account.
tip: Make it his routine: he presses the button, logs in to his kid account, and logs out himself when he is done.

cards.q: The tablet is all the way off. Which button turns it on?
cards.note: The power button is usually on the top or the side. One press and the screen lights up.

cards.q: You press the power button and the tablet takes a little while to start. What is it doing?
cards.note: Grown-ups say it is booting up. The computer is waking every part up, so give it a moment.

cards.q: You want to turn the tablet all the way off. What do you do to the power button?
cards.note: A quick press only puts it to sleep, but holding the button down turns it all the way off. Ask a grown-up to show you.

cards.q: Turning a computer all the way off has a name. What is it called?
cards.note: Shutting down closes everything and turns the power off. Shut down before a long trip or when a grown-up says so.

cards.q: You press the power button quickly and the screen goes dark. Is the tablet off or asleep?
cards.note: A quick press is sleep. The screen is dark, but the tablet is still on, resting and ready.

cards.q: A tablet goes to sleep when nobody uses it for a while. Why does it sleep?
cards.note: Sleep saves battery while the tablet waits for you. Press once and it wakes up right where you were.

cards.q: The screen went dark by itself while you were reading. How do you wake it up?
cards.note: One press on the power button or a tap on the screen wakes a sleeping tablet. No shaking needed.

cards.q: You shut down the laptop. What happens to the apps you had open?
cards.note: Shut down closes all the apps, but sleep keeps them open. Save your work before you shut down.

cards.q: A grown-up plugs in the charger and a tiny light comes on. What does the light mean?
cards.note: The little light says charging. When the battery is full, the light may change color or turn off.

cards.q: Logging in means telling the computer something. What do you tell it?
cards.note: Logging in tells the computer who you are, with your name and password, so it shows your things.

cards.q: A grown-up unlocks the phone with a look or a touch. What is the phone checking?
cards.note: Some phones check a face or a fingerprint instead of a typed password. It is still a kind of password.

cards.q: Before you log in, you see a screen with a big clock on it. What is it called?
cards.note: The lock screen shows the time but keeps your things locked until the right person logs in.

cards.q: You log out when you are done. Who can use your account then?
cards.note: Nobody. Logging out closes your account so the next person cannot see or change your things.

cards.q: The tablet has a grown-up account and a kid account. Which one is yours?
cards.note: A kid account is set up just for you. The grown-up account is for grown-up jobs, so leave it alone.

cards.q: What does a kid account show you?
cards.note: A kid account shows the games and apps your grown-ups picked for you and hides the rest.

cards.q: A grown-up's account is open on the screen. What do you do?
cards.note: Someone else's account is theirs. Ask first, and never tap around in a grown-up's work.

cards.q: You are about to close the laptop lid. What do you check first?
cards.note: Check that your drawing or story is saved. Then close the lid and the laptop goes to sleep.

cards.q: You close the laptop lid. What does the laptop do?
cards.note: Closing the lid puts a laptop to sleep. Open it and press a key or the button to wake it.
